title: Saudi to introduce domestic minimum top-up tax for multinationals effective January
summary: The tax applies to constituent entities of MNE groups that have consolidated annual revenues of at least 750mln euro or its equivalent in Saudi riyal

Riyadh skyline, financial district seen along King Fahd Road, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Image used for illustrative purpose. Getty Images

The tax applies to constituent entities of MNE groups that have consolidated annual revenues of at least 750mln euro or its equivalent in Saudi riyal

Staff Writer ,  Saudi Gazette

RIYADH — The Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) has announced that it will start implementing the domestic minimum top-up tax (DMTT) effective January 1, 2027. 

The tax applies to constituent entities of multinational enterprise (MNE) groups that have consolidated annual revenues of at least 750 million euro or its equivalent in Saudi riyal.

The authority clarified that the tax will apply to entities meeting this revenue threshold according to the consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent entity in at least two of the four fiscal years preceding the year in which the tax is applied.

The scope of application is limited to entities that meet the eligibility criteria within multinational groups and does not extend to all companies operating in Saudi Arabia. Accordingly, it excludes purely domestic companies that do not have branches outside Saudi Arabia or do not belong to a covered MNE group.

The tax is based on the consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent entity in at least two of the four fiscal years preceding the fiscal year in which the tax applies, in a step aimed at protecting Saudi Arabia's tax rights and keeping pace with international tax developments.

According to a press release issued by the ZATCA on Thursday, this tax comes within the framework of international trends aimed at establishing global minimum tax rules under Pillar Two, led by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the G20, thereby contributing to the protection of the Kingdom's tax rights on profits generated within its jurisdiction by the covered MNE groups.

ZATCA explained that the DMTT allows for the collection of the top-up tax within the Kingdom on profits whenever the effective tax rate falls below the established global minimum threshold of 15 percent, in accordance with the relevant rules. This percentage refers to the minimum effective tax rate on profits and is not a rate levied on the total revenues of companies.

The authority stated that the implementation of the DMTT aligns with international efforts aimed at enhancing tax fairness and ensuring that profits are subject to the global minimum tax in the countries where they are generated, supporting the protection of states' tax rights and enhancing the consistency of tax laws with international standards.

ZATCA has invited targeted MNE entities and those seeking further information to reach out through its unified call center number 19993 (operating 24/7), the "Ask ZATCA" account on X @Zatca_care, via email at [email protected], or through the live chat feature on ZATCA's website ‏Zatca.gov.sa .
